He was about one meter sixty nine. Average, or even a bit taller than average, for a Frenchman of his time.
So where did the myth come from?
First, the numbers. French inches were longer than British inches.
So when his height was written as five feet two in French units, the British read it as tiny.
Second, the British loved to mock him. Cartoonists drew him as a tiny, angry man throwing tantrums.
And third, his nickname, the little corporal, was actually a term of affection from his soldiers.
He was also usually surrounded by his Imperial Guard, who had to be tall to join.
So the shortest thing about Napoleon was his temper.
